To summarize, the key findings of our research, stated in one sentence that includes all relevant information, are that
the nature of the DM has a significant impact on the fragmentation of filaments and on the properties of the resulting haloes.
the fragmentation of a warm-dark-matter (WDM) filament is different from the fragmentation of a cold-dark-matter (CDM) filament.
WDM filamentary structures fragment into gravitationally bound objects in a top-down way, and that the Jeans mass of these objects is in the range 10 9 - 10 10 M⊙.
In summary, our research is concerned with
the formation of dwarf galaxies, which are thought to constitute the most abundant class of galaxies in the Universe, and with the question of how they are formed.
the question whether the nature of the dominant matter component in the universe, dark matter, can be constrained by the properties of dwarf galaxies.
the question whether or not the nature of the Dark Matter affects the formation of dwarf galaxies and their clustering properties.
In summary, a comprehensive and detailed conclusive statement would be that
the WDM filaments are more filamentary, less spherical, and less concentrated than the CDM counterparts, but they have a similar number of halos and similar mass distribution.
WDM is more filamentary, more clumpy, more inhomogeneous, more hierarchical and, in the end, more complex than the standard CDM scenario.
WDM filamaments fragment in a top-down manner, whereas CDM ones fragment in a bottom-up fashion.
A comprehensive summary for our work would be that
WDM filamentos are not only different from CDM filamentos, but also from each other.

WDM differs significantly from CDM only on the scales where CDM haloes are predicted to form late, i.e. below 10 9-10 10 M⊙, and that the nature of the DM has a significant impact on the properties of dwarf galaxies.
the formation of low-mass dark matter haloes in WDM is more filament-like than in CDM, and that the mass of haloes in WMD is higher than in CDM at a given epoch.
The main takeaway from our work is that

, while WDM is able to reproduce many observed features of galaxies and galaxy groups, it is unable to form the most massive galaxies, which are instead predicted to be much less massive in WDM than CDM.
the nature of the DM particle has a profound influence on the formation history of low-mass galaxies.
the nature of the DM is not just an issue for cosmology, but also for galaxy formation.
